ranked.headline: Generative and graph-based models infer regulatory structure from single-cell data
ranked.summary: Optimal transport and graph attention now link single-cell snapshots, perturbations, and spatial maps to regulatory and cell-state inference.

ranked.headline: Epigenomic and mutational readouts resolve origin, repair and instability in cancer
ranked.summary: Single-cell sequencing, CRISPR mutational spectra and epigenomic profiles are now used to probe instability, repair and origin in cancer.

ranked.headline: Penalized and goal-directed models stratify biology from high-dimensional omics data
ranked.summary: Omics models are increasingly tailored to explicit outcomes, such as ordinal endpoints and goal-directed partitioning, rather than generic classifiers.

ranked.headline: Simulation and force-field refinements resolve protein energy landscapes and dynamics
ranked.summary: Refined force fields, coarse-grained parameters and membrane-embedded simulations now capture conformational energetics in proteins and condensates.

ranked.headline: Learned representations drive compound, protein, and toxicity prediction across tasks
ranked.summary: Representation learning now extends from pairwise interaction prediction to morphology synthesis, toxicity, and active phenotype screening.

ranked.headline: Benchmarked sequencing and informatics tools span nanopore, TCR, and virus discovery
ranked.summary: Sequencing and informatics tools are now evaluated against established reference methods, including bulk and 10x single-cell TCR-seq.

ranked.headline: Topological and network context used to infer disease-linked molecular features
ranked.summary: Omics analyses are increasingly built on topology and network embeddings to capture disease-associated structure beyond pairwise comparison.

ranked.headline: Long-read isoform resolution is refining transcript annotation and splicing regulation
ranked.summary: Long-read and single-cell methods now resolve individual isoforms and haplotypes, enabling isoform-level annotation and regulatory inference.

ranked.headline: Software pipelines turn raw omics reads into analysis-ready matrices and features
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications release open-source tools that convert raw spatial, surface-marker, and multiomics data into analysis-ready form.

ranked.headline: Calibrated models and deep learning refine copy number and variant effect calls
ranked.summary: Residue- and proteome-scale calibration of variant predictors is now being coupled to clinical and pharmacogenomic annotation layers.

ranked.headline: Convergence, introgression, and indel dynamics shape animal genome evolution
ranked.summary: Recent work applies comparative statistics across fish, birds, and modeling of conserved DNA to test evolutionary signatures at genome scale.

ranked.headline: Fusing pretrained protein embeddings with structural features for prediction tasks
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers pair protein language model or inverse-folding embeddings with structural modules for binding, epitope, and search tasks.

ranked.headline: Graph and tree-based frameworks for comparative genomic and phylogenetic inference
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs sequence-graph representations with statistical corrections and confidence measures for metagenomic and phylogenomic analyses.

ranked.headline: Simulation models link mutations, menopause, and mitochondria to aging and tumor onset
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply mechanistic simulation and survival modeling to aging and cancer at cell, tissue, and lifespan scales.

ranked.headline: Joint alignment and optimal transport couple spatial slices and gene networks
ranked.summary: November 2025 preprints pair shared low-dimensional embeddings with transport-based alignment across spatial slices and cancer network states.

ranked.headline: Learned representations and generative models for biomolecular structure and dynamics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple physically structured inputs with learned representations and generators for conformational data and binding kinetics.

ranked.headline: Observation frames of wastewater, serology and trials shape pathogen inference methods
ranked.summary: Wastewater RNA, longitudinal microbiome, ICU physiological and paired serology data each now get estimators matched to their observation structure.

ranked.headline: Structure-guided computational design of peptides, enzymes, and antibodies
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and one published study apply structure-conditioned design to peptides, enzymes, antibodies, and small-molecule hit-to-lead work.

ranked.headline: Taxonomy and protein-level models for genome annotation and microbiome trait prediction
ranked.summary: Language and deep learning models are now benchmarked and applied to microbial phenotypes, viral genomes, and eukaryotic gene models.

ranked.headline: Statistical models of spatial dependence in gene co-expression and chromatin structure
ranked.summary: Spatial and single-cell datasets now demand statistics that respect tissue geometry, measurement error, and atlas alignment.

ranked.headline: Statistical models link molecular QTLs across tissues, cell types and isoforms
ranked.summary: Recent methods integrate bulk, single-cell, multi-tissue, and isoform-level QTL data to strengthen GWAS-linked inference.

ranked.headline: Compressed indexes enable k-mer search, FASTQ parsing and mass-spec queries at scale
ranked.summary: Million-genome k-mer search and parallel gzipped FASTQ parsing are being made feasible on commodity hardware without recompressing the source data.

ranked.headline: Scalable algorithms for ancestry, species trees, diversity and genome alignment
ranked.summary: Genome and species datasets now reach thousands of haplotypes and 100,000 taxa, pushing inference tools toward low memory and parallel execution.

ranked.headline: Protein language model embeddings encode motifs, local structure and remote homology
ranked.summary: Pretrained protein language model embeddings are now being used directly for motif localization, structural similarity inference and alphabet design.

ranked.headline: Likelihood-free and Bayesian calibration of epidemic and phylodynamic models
ranked.summary: Mechanistic epidemic and phylodynamic models are now fit to diverse data types, making inference validity and model comparison central questions.

ranked.headline: Learned models recover molecular information lost to missingness, sparsity, and pooling
ranked.summary: Learned models now encode missingness, sparsity, and multiplexing limits directly within omics inference workflows.

ranked.headline: Brain models move beyond pairwise connectivity to higher-order and manifold descriptions
ranked.summary: Combinatorial complexes, control-based timescales, and neural manifolds now probe higher-order and dynamical structure beyond pairwise connectivity.

ranked.headline: Phase-plane model links in vitro aggregation kinetics to cell-level bistability
ranked.summary: Explicit bistability and oscillatory outputs now link in vitro kinetics and behavior-adaptive dynamics to disease-relevant state transitions.

ranked.headline: Interpretable sequence models reveal motif features driving regulatory predictions
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and published work tie regulatory predictions to explicit motif, positional, and paired-sequence features.

ranked.headline: Microbiome bioinformatics tools judged against explicit benchmarks and orthogonal checks
ranked.summary: Recent microbiome and genomics tool papers report validation against benchmarks or defined criteria, making evaluation design a shared concern.

ranked.headline: Isoform-aware GRNs, entropy-based specificity, and spike-in-normalized ChIP-seq
ranked.summary: Recent work extends regulatory network inference, gene specificity scoring, and normalization toward isoform- and chromatin-level resolution.

ranked.headline: Ancestry QC, differentiable GBLUP, and haplotype-resolved pangenome genotyping tools
ranked.summary: New preprints extend population-genetic inference to ancestry QC, learned genomic prediction, and diploid phasing on pangenome graphs.

ranked.headline: Pangenome graphs and site-based mutation dynamics resolve pathogen genomic variation
ranked.summary: Graph-based and phylogeny-free variant methods are improving variant detection and lineage surveillance across viral and bacterial pathogen genomes.

ranked.headline: Language models and optimization steer RNA sequence design toward target structures
ranked.summary: Preprints now couple conditional nucleic acid generation to explicit structural, binding, and multi-target objectives rather than sequence recovery alone.

ranked.headline: Learned models now segment cryo-ET membranes and track proteins in 4D microscopy
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications introduce segmentation, foundation-model and structural-resource tools for cryo-EM, cryo-ET and protein imaging workflows.

ranked.headline: Stochastic models link local cellular and molecular rules to population-level outcomes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints use stochastic models to explain how local noisy rules produce global distributions and chemotactic search outcomes.

ranked.headline: Mycobacterium tuberculosis uses intrinsically disordered, fast evolving proteins to interact with conserved host factors.
ranked.summary: Benchmarks disorder predictors; links M. tuberculosis IDRs to virulence and host interactions across 540 bacteria; releases IDR database.

ranked.headline: Tools expose gene loss, parental ancestry, and recombination graphs for inspection
ranked.summary: Genome assemblies, breeding crosses, and inferred genealogies increasingly need interpretable, interactive visual readouts alongside automated computation.

ranked.headline: Allosteric connectivity underlies p53 Y220C stabilizer action in microsecond simulations
ranked.summary: Long-timescale simulations now resolve how p53 Y220C stabilizers restore allosteric networks and how XPD translocates along ssDNA.

ranked.headline: Computational separation of target protein contributions from confounding background
ranked.summary: Complex imaging and mass spectrometry data mix target and background contributions, so these preprints add computational separation steps.
